decisive_items: bilateral naevus flammeus along the ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of the trigeminal nerve
choroidal thickness of 2.2 mm in the right eye versus 1.4 mm in the left
intraocular pressure measured by Icare tonometry was 22 mm Hg in the right eye and 12 mm Hg in the left
response.rationale: Facial port-wine stain in V1/V2 distribution with ipsilateral glaucoma and diffuse choroidal thickening is characteristic of Sturge-Weber syndrome even without leptomeningeal involvement. Ocular melanocytosis explains the iris/trabecular pigmentation but not the facial angioma.

rejected.why: Explains iris hyperpigmentation, trabecular pigmentation, and dark choroid, but does not account for the facial naevus flammeus/angioma.
Glaucoma is a secondary complication of the underlying syndrome, not the primary diagnosis, and does not explain the facial angioma or choroidal thickening.
